business_problem: Honda needed a faster way to transfer skilled engineering knowledge into its Advanced Expert System because converting internal PowerPoint materials into reusable knowledge models for vehicle-development reviews was too manual and slow to scale across thousands of parts.
solution_summary: Honda worked with IBM to use generative AI for extracting engineering know-how from Microsoft PowerPoint materials and turning it into reusable knowledge for its Advanced Expert System. The source documents contained diagrams and graphs but relatively little text, which made them difficult to reuse with conventional AI techniques. IBM proposed a multimodal approach in IBM watsonx.ai that converts graphical and diagram-heavy content into text, stores the resulting know-how in a database, and then supports retrieval-augmented-generation-style knowledge access. A pilot run from November to December 2023 validated the approach. The resulting architecture lets Honda move from manually creating handbooks and knowledge models over multi-year timelines toward AI-assisted documentation modeling that can surface engineering guidance faster, reduce rework in collision-safety simulation reviews, and broaden reuse of expert knowledge across the development organization.
